Strong Jobs Report Revives December Rate Hike Bets

Zandi called it "a really solid report," but said "a lot of noise" in it overstates the labor market’s strength. Because last month’s job numbers were "very weak," he said, "the reality is probably somewhere in between."

Inflation "still remains elevated," he said, though core CPI, due next week, looks like it will decelerate. Fed members are "still very nervous about the high rates of inflation," and with this jobs number, "they’ve got latitude to raise rates," said Zandi. "I think there’s very high probability they hike in December," he said.
Housing Freeze, Market Weakness And AI Inflation

Zandi said he is "less sure" about a rate hike beyond December, because higher interest rates and a weaker stock market should soften the labor market and the economy, and inflation should come down as long as the Iran war "goes in the right direction." "So this might be one more rate hike and that’s the end of it," he said, adding that there could be "another rate hike or two in 2027" if not. He said fixed mortgage rates over 7% have "really done a number on the housing market," which was already in a "deep freeze" and is now "kind of frozen solid," and that the S&P has "essentially gone nowhere" for six months, which should take "a little bit of steam out of wealth and consumer spending."

Asked what a slowdown in data center construction would mean for the economy, Zandi said the AI boom is currently juicing growth through spending and higher stock prices, and also adds to inflation through electricity, chips and consumer electronics. If AI cools off, he said, the Fed may not need the same number of rate hikes, and a cool-off "might be the best thing for the economy and for the AI industry" because the industry feels like it is "getting ahead of itself."
